answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity as a refundable stake that only earns back as a verified history accrues. A clone begins at the reputational nadir, holding no prior thread of attested work. To cross the bridge into the trusted set it must post fresh collateral and slowly rebuild standing through peer-countersigned tasks. Because each fake needs its own stake and its own earned thread, forging N identities costs N times the capital and time, so sybil fleets stall at the nadir.
